title: Research Intake OCR Fallback
question: How does MNEMOS handle scanned PDFs?
short_answer: The research intake tool tries pypdf extraction first. If PDF text density is below the configured threshold, it treats the file as scanned and routes extraction to the optional Docling OCR fallback, recording extraction method metadata for downstream evidence.

evidence_used.claim_supported: PDF extraction uses pypdf first and routes low-text-density scanned PDFs to Docling OCR when available.
evidence_used.public_safe_summary: Code records extraction method, page count, chars per page, source URI, file hash, page range metadata, and claim boundary.

evidence_used.claim_supported: Tests cover scanned PDF routing to Docling OCR fallback, text PDFs staying on pypdf, and PDF chunks carrying page start/end metadata.
evidence_used.public_safe_summary: Unit tests validate the fallback branch and metadata behavior without requiring a live public upload path.

evidence_used.claim_supported: Research Intake UI is the user-facing way to put PDFs and other artifacts into MNEMOS before asking questions.
evidence_used.public_safe_summary: Documents the local intake workflow and notes timeout/batch-size tuning for large PDFs.

limitations: This trace describes the static behavior of the intake code and tests.

Large PDFs may need timeout or batch-size tuning in local workflows.
